title: Cardinality of a transcendence basis over a countable field
statement: Let $F\to K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with $F$ countable, meaning $|F|\leq\aleph_0$, and $K$ an uncountable algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], meaning $\aleph_0<|K|$. Let $b:I\to K$ be a transcendence basis over $F$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Then $|I|=|K|$, with cardinalities compared in a common universe. Here $|S|$ denotes set cardinality and $\aleph_0=|\mathbf N|$.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: "Each basis has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$" and the ensuing countable-base cardinality argument. Mathlib/FieldTheory/IsAlgClosed/Classification.lean:122-151; transcendence basis means Stacks Fields Definition 030E (definition-transcendence).

mathlib_searches.query: A transcendence basis of an uncountable algebraically closed field over a countable field has the cardinality of the field
Over a countable field the cardinality of a transcendence basis of an uncountable algebraically closed field equals the cardinality of that field

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take R=F, K=K, v=b, hR the countability hypothesis and hK uncountability; a field is a nontrivial commutative ring. The theorem gives lift #K = lift #I, hence the symmetric equality in the statement. Same-universe version at line 149. Both types and proofs read.
